scene: On the captured merchant sloop's deck in bright sun, the Surgeon (thin man of about forty, gray hair tied back with a black ribbon, clean-shaven, plain black coat over a white shirt, long brown leather apron) hugs his wooden medicine chest with brass corners to his chest, eyes wide and sweating, while the Captain (black tricorn, full brown beard, burgundy long coat) pulls on one handle and the Quartermaster (dark-brown wavy hair, light stubble, white shirt, dark-brown waistcoat) pulls on the other. A few glass jars and rolled bandages tumble out of the half-open lid. Tension: the crew wants the chest more than the man.

Below deck by warm lantern light, the Crewmate (black hair with a small tail, olive shirt) thrusts his bandaged hand toward the camera with an outraged, greedy face, while the Surgeon in his leather apron stands beside him holding a small pewter syringe and a brown glass bottle, staring at a hand-painted wooden board nailed to the bulkhead that shows a simple drawing of an arm, a leg and an eye next to stacks of coins. Tom (navy waistcoat, no hat) peeks in from the ladder, counting his own fingers. No real logos or readable words on the board except numbers.
